unresolved: L20, the label in the left margin: only «et M)» is in the image, which ends at the left edge of the page; by the label «(O)» of the right column and the manuscripts whose text the left column gives, it is probably «(C et M)».
observations: The page number «7» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. L01-L12 end chapter 5 (p. 6, JP2 0038). L03: the vertical bar between «annorum» and «pla-» marks the beginning of fol. 84 verso of M, which the note in the right margin, «M 84v», names. L13: the heading of chapter 6, in bold, centred, with «C 44v, O 101r» in the right margin.

L19: «Cap. 7.», in bold, centred. L20-L39: chapter 7 is printed in two columns, as Suter says on p. XIII (JP2 0017, L12-L14): on the left the text of C and M, on the right that of O, each with its own heading in bold (L20-L22, L30-L31); the columns are transcribed one after the other, the left first (L20-L29), then the right (L30-L39). Beside the first line of each heading the sigla stand in the margin: «(O)» in the right margin; in the left margin the label is cut off at the left edge of the image, the visible part reading «et M)», the e of «et» itself cut.

L18: «descrescit», so printed in the text and in the lemma of note 24, for decrescit; transcribed as printed. L21: «elwacat» in italics in the text; the headings have «elwacat» (left) and «elwazat» (right) in the bold of the headings.

N10: the t of «translatio» is printed without its crossbar and the last e of «aperte» with its bar faint; transcribed as the letters they are. N07: the omission in the lemma is printed as five points. N08: «O.—», the dash set close.
The semicolon of N07 and the colon of N09 stand after the thin space of the edition (8 and 10 px measured).

critical_notes.evidence: the chapter headings print the abbreviation with its point, «Cap. 5.» (p. 6), «Cap. 7.» (L19); after «Cap» of chapter 6 the point is not printed

the sentence of the right column runs on, «per numerum annorum collectorum, deinde per numerum annorum planorum praeteritorum»; the full stop before the lower-case «deinde» stands where a comma is needed
